items.title: 67750_Sippie Wallace oral history interview
items.q: I had a little girl named Lil Creole. Her name was Creole, you know, and she wouldn't play with me because I wouldn't put her name on the record.

ctx.x: See, it was a long time before I got Herschel. See, I had to get Herschel -- I had to break Herschel in. See, I didn't have Herschel, my little brother Herschel, to play with me (unintelligible). I had a little girl named Lil Creole. Her name was Creole, you know, and she wouldn't play with me because I wouldn't put her name on the record. See, I could tell somebody (unintelligible).
Well now, you played in 1924 with Clarence Williams?

items.title: 67750_Sippie Wallace oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer asks about 'Lillby' and a 'jealous woman', but the interviewee's response discusses interactions with Louis Armstrong and a woman who spoke to her, without explicitly identifying Lillby or describing a personal relationship with Lillby.

ctx.x: Just talking to (unintelligible). Matt was scared -- my husband was named Matt -- Matt was scared to death. Louis say, "Go on now, (inaudible)." So my brother Herschel played the piano and so Herschel was playing Herschel ______ and Louis said, "Special." I said, "Lord, it must have been from --" I said, "It must be from my man." (Unintelligible) and he was (unintelligible). And oh, Louis sure did go to town with that song and I'm telling you the truth.
You know, you were saying about Lillby (PHONETIC) and the jealous woman, how did you know that?
